concerns.text: Task T005a explicitly generates a 'deterministic synthetic gold standard' to replace manual annotation if real data is missing. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) and Principle VI (Failure-Mode Structural Annotation) which mandate that results must be reproducible from the canonical ARC-Bench dataset, not synthetic fallbacks. The task relaxes the requirement for real-data validation.

Task T011c implements a 'Mock Data Generator' fallback if T011b fails. This silently relaxes FR-001 and FR-002 which require the system to ingest and process the ARC-Bench dataset. Allowing the pipeline to proceed with mock data when real data ingestion fails violates the core research constraint of using verified empirical data.

Task T011b states: 'The mapping from raw_error_log to annotated_structural_feature is performed by a deterministic rule set (regex patterns and keyword heuristics)... to simulate the Human-in-the-Loop annotation process.' This violates Constitution Principle VI which requires explicit annotation of failure transcripts. Simulating the annotation with regex heuristics instead of performing the required Human-in-the-Loop or verified LLM annotation process weakens the FR-001 requirement for valid structural feature labeling.

Task T021 orchestrates baseline execution on an external CI job but does not include a task to implement the `baseline_agent.py` script referenced in T021b. This creates a gap where the FR-004 requirement to 'execute... the full AutoResearchClaw baseline agent' cannot be satisfied because the agent logic is missing from the task list.

Task T080 is marked as incomplete (`[ ]`) and references a schema file (`distilled_rule.schema.yaml`) that T006b creates, but the task itself is not executed in the main orchestration (T060). This leaves the FR-002 requirement for schema validation of the rule library unenforced in the final pipeline, creating a silent relaxation of the validation constraint.

Tasks T029a, T029c, and T029h all describe implementing the same Tobit Regression logic for censored data. This redundancy creates ambiguity in the execution order and verification logic. More critically, the split implementation risks inconsistent handling of censored data (SC-001), potentially violating the requirement for a unified, correct statistical treatment of censored 'Time-to-Pivot' values.
